paragraphs.en: Every Saturday, Tom and his Uzbek friend Jamshid go to Chorsu Bazaar in Tashkent. Tom is from England. He is a teacher at a language school.
paragraphs.uz: Har shanba kuni Tom va uning o'zbek do'sti Jamshid Toshkentdagi Chorsu bozoriga borishadi. Tom Angliyadan. U til maktabida o'qituvchi.

paragraphs.en: The bazaar is very big and there are a lot of people. There are fruits, vegetables, bread, spices and sweets. Tom loves the colours and the smells.
paragraphs.uz: Bozor juda katta va odam ko'p. U yerda mevalar, sabzavotlar, non, ziravorlar va shirinliklar bor. Tom ranglar va hidlarni juda yaxshi ko'radi.

paragraphs.en: "How much are these melons?" Tom asks in Uzbek. The man smiles. "Twenty thousand," he says. "That's expensive!" says Jamshid. "Fifteen?" The man laughs. "OK, fifteen for you."
paragraphs.uz: "Bu qovunlar qancha?" — so'raydi Tom o'zbekcha. Sotuvchi jilmayadi. "Yigirma ming," deydi u. "Qimmat-ku!" — deydi Jamshid. "O'n besh?" Sotuvchi kuladi. "Xo'p, sizga o'n besh."

paragraphs.en: Then they buy hot bread — non — and some grapes. Tom's bag is very heavy now. They sit in a small café and drink green tea.
paragraphs.uz: Keyin ular issiq non va biroz uzum sotib olishadi. Tomning sumkasi endi juda og'ir. Ular kichkina choyxonada o'tirib, ko'k choy ichishadi.

paragraphs.en: "I love Saturdays," Tom says. "Me too," says Jamshid. "See you next week!"
paragraphs.uz: "Shanbalarni yaxshi ko'raman," deydi Tom. "Men ham," deydi Jamshid. "Kelasi hafta ko'rishamiz!"

questions.q: How much do they pay for the melons?
What do they drink in the café?
